handbookNote: North Dakota Century Code Chapter 44-06.1 (Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts / RULONA), NDCC 44-06.1-01 through 44-06.1-30 including the two ".1"-numbered add-on sections (44-06.1-13.1 remote notarization, 44-06.1-16.1 journals) -- fetched directly from ndlegis.gov. Classification: North Dakota is an APPLICATION-ONLY notary state, confirmed against both NNA guidance and the full statute text -- there is no exam and no mandatory training course anywhere in the chapter; commissioning is by application to the secretary of state (44-06.1-20) with an oath and a surety bond, with no testing requirement of any kind. The prior Chapter 44-06 was repealed effective August 1, 2011 and fully replaced by this RULONA adoption. Notable statutory quirks documented in this track: (1) a codified $5.00-per-notarial-act fee cap at 44-06.1-28(1), unusually low and explicit compared to most states, with separate travel/technology fees allowed only under advance-agreement and disclosure conditions; (2) border-county reciprocity at 44-06.1-20(2)(c), allowing residents of a county in a neighboring state to qualify for an ND commission if that state extends similar reciprocity to ND border-county residents; (3) a 4-year bar on reapplying for a commission after revocation, per 44-06.1-21(2); (4) a $7,500 surety bond/assurance requirement at 44-06.1-20(4); (5) a fully built-out remote online notarization regime at 44-06.1-13.1 with dual identity-proofing pathways (personal knowledge, credible-witness oath, or two types of identity proofing) and a 10-year audiovisual-recording retention requirement; (6) a journal mandate at 44-06.1-16.1 that -- unlike many other RULONA states -- is tied specifically to remote notarial acts rather than all notarial acts generally. Content depth rationale: with no exam and no training curriculum to ground content against, this track is built as grounded self-study/reference practice questions drawn directly from the 30-operative-section statute itself, each citing a specific 44-06.1-xx subsection; 171 questions were authored across 12 topic buckets covering every section of the chapter (definitions, notarial act requirements/identification, interstate/tribal/federal/foreign recognition, remote notarization, certificates/short forms, official stamp/stamping device, journals, vacancies/electronic records/database, commission qualifications, discipline/grounds/complaints, prohibited acts/UPL, and fees/name-change/administrative provisions) -- no filler or invented facts were added to hit a target count. Priced at $0.99 (2026-08-16 directive), matching this project's application-only-state tier: since ND has no confirmed graded assessment of any kind, this is education-only reference practice content, not exam prep, and is priced well below the $9.99 exam-state tier accordingly.
